subject: Reliability SLO follow-up: Redwood vs hyperscalers
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jared Coleman <jared@hyperscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: reliability / SLO discussion + next tests

Hi Jared —

Great to speak earlier — thanks for walking through your production concerns. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Call recap (short):
- Hyperscale.ai priority: production stability for real-time inference (low tail latency + minimal downtime) for user-facing features.
- Main evaluation axes: uptime/SLOs, rate limits & throttling behavior, error budgets & alerting, and failover/region fallback behavior.
- You want a comparison vs your current hyperscaler endpoints (AWS SageMaker/Bedrock) focused on real-world failover and degraded-mode behavior.

Redwood differentiators (high-level):
- Deterministic SLOs with per-route availability tracking and historical error budgeting (we expose per-route 5xx% + per-minute latency percentiles in Console).
- Rate limiting: token-bucket per-tenant with configurable burst and per-route quotas (not opaque per-IP quotas).
- Failover: automatic model-variant fallback + cross-region routing policies; prioritized by cost/latency tiers.
- Dedicated capacity option for predictable throughput (reserved GPUs) vs hosted which uses smart routing and autoscaling.

Proposed tests (we recommend):
1) 48-hour soak running production-weight traffic to validate sustained availability and error budget burn patterns.
2) High-concurrency burst test (simulate 10x normal concurrent requests) to observe throttling and tail latency.
3) Region-failover simulation (bring down primary region from load-balancer to observe automatic fallback and time-to-recover).
4) Rate-limit boundary tests: per-API-key burst behavior and graceful degradation responses.

Attachments: I attached an SLO comparison PDF and a light test-plan spreadsheet.

Action items / questions for you:
- Can you share a representative traffic profile (QPS, typical seq length, 99th latency target) for the endpoints you want tested?
- Do you want tests run against our hosted API first or set up a short Dedicated trial?
- Preferred window for tests: we’re available Mar 30–Apr 2 (PST) or Apr 6–8.

Next step: If you’re good, I’ll loop in Aditya (solutions engineer) to own the test-run and Marissa for SLO dashboard setup.

Thanks — talk soon,

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

Attachment: 2026-03-22-redwood-hyperscale-slo-comparison.pdf

From: Jared Coleman <jared@hyperscale.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: reliability / SLO discussion + next tests

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifying questions before we lock the test window:  \

1) Cross-region failover: when you say automatic fallback, what’s the recovery window we should expect? Is state (KV cache / warm KV) preserved or do we expect cold starts that impact latency?
2) Error budget definition: is that measured per-route per-minute 5xx% or aggregated daily? How do you surface a burn chart and alert thresholds?
3) Rate limits: is the token-bucket enforced per-API key or per-account? We have multiple product teams using the same account and need per-team isolation.
4) For fairness in comparison against our hyperscaler baseline (Bedrock), can you confirm the SLA number you measure to (99.9 vs 99.95) and whether you include transient DNS/provider interruptions in your availability calc?

Also — are there any rate-limit headers returned by the API we can use to programmatically back off?

If you can answer these first, we’ll circulate an internal slot preference and a list of traffic samples.

—Jared
Principal Infra Engineer | Hyperscale.ai
jared@hyperscale.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jared Coleman <jared@hyperscale.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: reliability / SLO discussion + next tests

Jared — thanks, great questions. Looping in Aditya to cover the technical specifics; I’ll answer at a high level first.

Short answers:
- Cross-region failover: typical failover detection + routing adjustment is under 60s for control-plane reroute in hosted mode; tail latency can spike during the first few requests (cold KV cache) but we use prefix/KV caching and warmup heuristics to reduce the impact. For Dedicated we can pre-provision warm hot-standby pools to get sub-10s failover.
- Error budget: we expose per-route per-minute 5xx% plus aggregated daily burn charts in Console. The SLO report groups by route and model; alerts are configurable (e.g., notify at 25%/50%/90% of daily budget burn). We do not count short-lived client DNS lookups as server 5xx — availability is measured server-side 5xx and timed-out responses.
- Rate limits: token-bucket is per-tenant by default, and we support per-API-key quotas for team isolation (recommended for multi-team customers). Burst is configurable and visible via rate-limit headers (x-rw-limit-remaining, x-rw-limit-reset, x-rw-limit-limit).
- SLA baseline: hosted API historical region-aggregated SLOs are commonly reported at 99.95% for core routes (we publish per-model/per-route p99 latency and availability charts). We will provide a 30-day historical report for the routes you plan to test so you can compare directly to Bedrock/SageMaker baselines.

Aditya — can you confirm the test plan details (I attached a spreadsheet) and note any logging/trace artifacts we’ll provide for post-test analysis?

Ben

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Jared Coleman <jared@hyperscale.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: reliability / SLO discussion + next tests

Hey Jared — quick note from the SE side. We reviewed your baseline thread and Bedrock metrics. Proposed test window confirmed: Apr 6–7 (we’ll do a staged set of runs across both days).

What we’ll provide during and after tests:
- Live SLO dashboard (read-only link) that shows per-route availability, 1m/5m/1h aggregates, and error-budget burn.
- Raw request logs (sampled) and a trace bundle for any 5xx/timeout you want us to inspect.
- Rate-limit headers are sent on every response: x-rw-limit-limit, x-rw-limit-remaining, x-rw-limit-reset. We’ll add a small example client snippet to the test-plan to demonstrate respectful backoff.
- For the region-failover test we’ll coordinate an orchestrated failover (we’ll momentarily withdraw the primary routing target) and measure time-to-failover and cold-start impact. Expect an initial tail spike; we’ll capture per-request latencies to quantify.

Next asks from your side (to finalize plan):
- A representative traffic CSV (timestamp, latency target, request payload size, QPS target) — please upload to the shared Drive link.
- List of API keys / team isolation mapping (we’ll create per-API-key quotas for the run).

I’ll attach the finalized test plan and a short script we use to run bursts. Happy to hop on a quick 30m runbook sync if useful.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
